item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 9, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until 8 p.m. Sunday, with heat index values expected to reach 108 degrees.
Heat advisory issued for Benton County through Sunday evening. The National Weather Service issued a heat advisory for Benton County from noon to 8 p.m. CDT on Sunday, with heat index values up to 108 expected.
Combined Committee of the Whole and City Council meets August 11. The council is asked to approve several zoning changes, a vacation of a right of way, and two grants for parks and traffic technology. Agendas for 1 other meeting this period are also published.
City council to consider street improvements and other business monday. Bentonville's combined Committee of the Whole and City Council will meet Monday at 6 p.m. The Finance Committee meets at 5 p.m. the same day.
Taziki's opens Rogers location. Taziki's Mediterranean Café opened at 1771 W. Pleasant Grove Road, Suite 104, in Rogers. The approximately 2,900-square-foot restaurant seats 85 guests and required $950,000 in investment.
Simmons Foods promotes Salmon to chief commercial officer. Siloam Springs-based Simmons Foods promoted Scott Salmon, president of Simmons Pet Food, to the newly created role of chief commercial officer. Jacob Rogers will succeed Salmon in his previous position.
Walton Family Foundation grants $599,139 to NWACC. The Walton Family Foundation provided a $599,139 grant to Northwest Arkansas Community College to expand its Learning, Improvement, Fun and Empowerment program.
Jessica DeBari named executive director of Community Creative Center. Fayetteville artist Jessica DeBari has been appointed executive director of Community Creative Center, a Fayetteville-based nonprofit arts organization.
Tyson Foods board declares quarterly dividend. The board of directors of Tyson Foods Inc. declared a quarterly dividend payment of 51 cents per share for Class A shareholders, payable on Dec. 15.
NWACC announces new dean of communications and arts division. Northwest Arkansas Community College announced a new leadership hire ahead of the fall semester.
Benton County named candidate for possible nuclear development. Arkansas lawmakers received results of a study on the feasibility of adding nuclear power to the state, which named a site in Northwest Arkansas as a candidate.
Benton County discusses one-cent sales tax proposal. Benton County held an intergovernmental meeting to discuss a proposed one-cent sales tax.
Two River Valley counties under burn ban amid wildfire risk. Amidst high heat and limited rain, some Northwest Arkansas and River Valley counties are under burn bans due to moderate wildfire risk.
Downtown Springdale Alliance hosts free picnic in the park series. Throughout August, the Downtown Springdale Alliance is hosting weekly Saturday events featuring food, music, and community gathering.
